title: Summarise a log file

cases.name: the example

files.app.log:
2025-05-03 10:00:01 INFO service started
2025-05-03 10:00:07 WARN cache is cold
2025-05-03 10:01:13 ERROR disk almost full
2025-05-03 10:02:40 INFO request served
2025-05-03 10:03:02 ERROR connection lost
2025-05-03 10:04:55 ERROR disk almost full
2025-05-03 10:05:00 INFO request served

cases.stdout:
lines: 7
INFO: 3
WARN: 1
ERROR: 3
top error: disk almost full

cases.name: no errors

files.quiet.log:
2025-01-01 09:00:00 INFO all good
2025-01-01 09:00:01 INFO still good

cases.stdout:
lines: 2
INFO: 2
WARN: 0
ERROR: 0
top error: none

cases.name: a tie goes to the alphabetically first message

files.tie.log:
d t ERROR zebra escaped
d t ERROR apple fell
d t ERROR zebra escaped
d t ERROR apple fell

cases.stdout:
lines: 4
INFO: 0
WARN: 0
ERROR: 4
top error: apple fell

cases.name: the level is matched as a field, not anywhere in the line

files.tricky.log:
d t INFO no ERROR here
d t WARN INFO was logged

cases.stdout:
lines: 2
INFO: 1
WARN: 1
ERROR: 0
top error: none

cases.name: an empty file
cases.stdout:
lines: 0
INFO: 0
WARN: 0
ERROR: 0
top error: none

hints: The level is the third field. awk '$3 == "ERROR"' matches it exactly, which grep on the whole line does not.
Count with awk and print n + 0, so that zero prints as 0 and the exit code stays 0.
For the message, take fields 4 to the end: cut -d' ' -f4-. Then sort | uniq -c, and sort by count descending and by message.
sort -k1,1nr -k2 sorts by the count (largest first) and then by the text.
